chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from al-'Azrami, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Whoever suffers illness for a night and accepts it with its (proper) acceptance, and renders his gratitude for it to Allah, it would be equivalent to sixty years of worship.'

My father said: 'So I said to him: What is its (proper) acceptance?' He said: 'That he is patient over it and does not inform (anyone) about what befell him in it; then when it is morning, he praises Allah for what had been.'

key_terms.شُكْر: shukr (gratitude) — rendering thanks to Allah for trials, recognizing them as divine gifts
key_terms.صَبْر: sabr (patience) — the foundational virtue of bearing hardship without distress or outward complaint
key_terms.عِبَادَة: worship — here used for spiritual reward, equating patient suffering to sustained devotional acts
key_terms.قَبُول: acceptance — here specifically meaning righteous, willing acceptance of divine decree without complaint

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for patiently accepting illness for one night according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that enduring a single night of illness with patience, acceptance, and gratitude to Allah carries the spiritual reward equivalent to sixty years of worship. The Imam defines 'proper acceptance' as a two-part practice: internal patience without complaint, and external discretion — not telling others about one's suffering — followed by praising Allah in the morning. This teaching addressed the Shia community during the Abbasid period, when believers faced hardship and oppression, encouraging them to transform suffering into spiritual merit rather than viewing it as punishment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Azramy, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who (suffers from) complaints (of an illness) for a night and he accepts it with an acceptance and pays his gratitude to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for it, would be like sixty years of his worship’.

My father said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is its acceptance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His being patient over it and not inform (anyone) with whatever was in it. So when it is the morning, he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon what was before’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from al-‘Arzamiy from his father who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that if a person becomes ill in a night, welcomes the night with whatever it has brought and gives thanks to Allah for that, it will be equal in reward to sixty years of worshipping.’
